title: CompletionReceipt
description: An assertion that a deliverable is ready for review, or that an execution ended without one. A host turn reaching status 'completed' is never by itself ready_for_review: turn completion is the trigger to look, the receipt is what gets verified. Each field names its producer, because a daemon observing turn/completed cannot supply what only the child knows.

eventId.description: For outcome ready_for_review: first 32 hex of sha256(relationshipId|generation|revisionHash|outcome) - product-level, so re-emitting one reviewable revision collapses. For execution-only outcomes there is no revision to identify, so it is sha256(relationshipId|generation|outcome|turnRef.turnId|attempt) - two interrupted turns in one generation stay two facts. The daemon's internal observation key (threadId, turnId, terminalStatus) never crosses this boundary; turnRef is its exported projection. Canonical derivation: fields joined by '|', integers rendered without padding, a null attempt rendered as the literal 'null', sha256 hex truncated to the first 32 characters.

attempt.description: The child's own re-run counter inside one generation. Producible only by the child; a daemon observation sets null.

revisionHash.description: sha256 over the sorted manifest of deliverable path+hash pairs. A turn id is not a revision. With no deliverable manifest this is the sentinel NO_DELIVERABLE = 64 zero characters.

outcome.description: Only ready_for_review asserts a reviewable product. blocked_needs_input is a child assertion: no terminal turn status identifies it, so a daemon may never synthesize it.

producer.description: child = the executing task asserted this outcome. daemon_observation = synthesized from a turn/completed notification, which can only ever report failed or interrupted.

turnRef.description: Must equal the observation that produced or accompanied this receipt.

manifest.description: The deliverable descriptors revisionHash was computed over, so a consumer can recompute it instead of trusting it. MANIFEST-CANON-01: each path is an absolute normalized POSIX path; entries are sorted byte-wise by that path; each serializes as '<absolutePath>:<lowercase hex sha256>'; entries are joined with a single newline and no trailing newline; revisionHash is the lowercase hex sha256 of that UTF-8 string. Relative paths are not permitted, because they produce a different hash for identical bytes. Every path must lie under the relationship's authorizedScope.artifactRoots. Required when outcome is ready_for_review; null for an execution-only outcome carrying the NO_DELIVERABLE sentinel.

path.description: Absolute normalized POSIX path (MANIFEST-CANON-01). A relative path is rejected: it would hash differently for identical bytes.

manifestRef.description: Resolvable path to a frozen copy of the manifest and its bytes, when the live files may move on. Used when the receipt must stay verifiable after a later revision.
